note: Wooded Lincoln Hills tract on the Mississippi south of Hannibal, once the site of a dynamite works. The primitive campground is beside the gravel boat-ramp lot on the river, east of Highway 79 across the railroad, with a privy; a gravel lane continues south along the bank. The area floods; do not drive onto flooded roads. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: page 'A concrete boat ramp and primitive campground are located along a portion of 1.5 miles of Mississippi River frontage'; brochure 'Camping is allowed on or adjacent to all graveled area parking lots', 14 days in 30; map (11/19/2018) Primitive Camping + P + privy at the ramp; GIS camp 201 / lot 127. Free/FCFS/no hookups/14 nights written manual. Pin fine. Riverview kept after measuring (~60 m through sparse trees, open view across the ramp lot). Phone matches.
flags: INCLUSION/FIT: area page 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites, Individual Campsites'; 'A concrete boat ramp and primitive campground are located along a portion of 1.5 miles of Mississippi River frontage.' Brochure: 'Camping is allowed on or adjacent to all graveled area parking lots... Stays are limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period. Groups of more than 10 campers require a special use permit.' Map marks Primitive Camping, Parking Lot, Privy and Disabled Accessible at the river end of the access road, with the Concrete Boat Ramp beside it; GIS camping point 201 sits ~25 m SE of lot 127 by a small structure (the privy). This is the 'adjacent to graveled lots' pattern with a mapped camping point and the page's own 'primitive campground', so it stays; the boat ramp shares the lot. Imagery: an open gravel lot ~70 x 35 m at the bank, with gravel lanes looping into the trees south of it and one running ~250 m SE along the bank. A 23-ft rig fits. Access: gravel road from Highway 79 crossing the Hannibal Sub railroad (map). Area page 'Notice: This area is subject to flooding. Check local conditions, and do not drive onto flooded roadways.'

WATERFRONT (stored riverview, kept, measured): camp point 201 is ~55-65 m from the Mississippi through sparse trees (0.46 m/px leaf-off frame), so riverfront fails (beyond 50 m, trees and the ramp lot between). The ramp lot is open gravel to the water's edge at the ramp, ~40 m from the camp point, so the river is in sight across the lot; the bank-side lane south of the lot runs 10-25 m from the water but is a lane, not a parking lot. Riverview holds; if AWH reads the summer canopy as blocking the view from the camp itself, it would go down to not waterfront.
PHONE: area page and brochure '(573) 248-2530' match; the brochure also gives Ted Shanks Conservation Area (573) 754-6171.
Season (manual, year-round) left as stored; the flooding notice is in the note.
Note rewritten: acreage, generic MDC text, the 14-day limit (now booking.max_stay_nights) and directions dropped; the campground's place and the flooding notice put in.
